Level 1 (STATIC_ANALYSIS) is a two-line block with no set -e/set -euo pipefail, no && chain, and no || exit 1 on either line: `node --check scripts/generate-final-report.mjs` then `npm run validate`. A bash block with no set -e returns the exit code of only its LAST command; if node --check fails but npm run validate (the last line) succeeds, the block exits 0 and the syntax-check failure is silently masked - the exact 'non-propagating block' trap plan-writer.md Hard Constraint #11 item 2 itself names. Fix: prepend `set -euo pipefail`, or chain as `node --check scripts/generate-final-report.mjs && npm run validate`.

Level 1's original always-PASS masking defect is fixed (set -euo pipefail now present; verified). However, independent verification surfaced a NEW always-FAIL defect in Level 3(b): buildMarkdown unconditionally appends a live-timestamped footer at scripts/generate-final-report.mjs line 495 (a template literal embedding new Date().toISOString() and reportsDir), and Level 3(b) compares two separately spawned process runs' full output via a raw assert.equal(after, before, ...) with zero normalization anywhere in the script. Because the two spawnSync calls run sequentially at genuinely different wall-clock moments, the embedded ISO timestamp differs between before and after even when the underlying script content is byte-identical, so the assertion throws unconditionally - confirmed by source trace (spawnSync is synchronous and sequential, never simultaneous; reportsDir itself is stable within a fixture so it is specifically the timestamp at fault) and corroborated by an empirical repro against the current unmodified tree showing two footers roughly 70ms apart. This is the plan's only gate on the binding AC-A4 byte-identical-output guarantee, so an always-failing gate here is worse than a cosmetic always-pass: it either blocks a correct implementation or trains the gate to be ignored. Fix: normalize only the timestamp substring before comparing - the reportsDir portion of the footer needs no normalization since it is already stable within a fixture; do not exclude the footer or any other region from comparison wholesale, since the table/Scope-column/approval-line content that region-if-broadened would hide is exactly what AC-A4 must keep covered. Independently re-verified the 3 per-task VALIDATE blocks are NOT vulnerable to this or the masking defect: Task 1 uses assert.match against narrow table-row regexes rather than whole-document equality and only runs the post-fix script once (no before/after comparison at all); Tasks 2 and 3 assert only on res.stderr, which never contains the markdown footer; none of the 4 node -e scripts wrap any assert call in try/catch, so a real failure always propagates as a non-zero exit.

Both Task 2's and Task 3's own per-task VALIDATE commands cannot pass even against a fully correct implementation, independent of the Level 1 / Level 3(b) defects already fixed in prior passes. Root cause, traced against the current unmodified scripts/generate-final-report.mjs: loadVisualApprovalLine (the function holding both tasks' target catch blocks) is invoked only when phaseScopes.get(phase) is non-null (source line 483: 'if (phaseScopes.get(phase) == null) continue;', immediately guarding the line-484 call to loadVisualApprovalLine(reportsDir, phase)), and phaseScopes.get(phase) is non-null only when loadPhaseScopes finds and reads a real plan file under <plansRoot>/plans/ (or /plans/completed/) whose content matches the phase_scope regex. Neither Task 2's fixture (plan lines 236-241) nor Task 3's fixture (plan lines 285-290) ever creates a PRPs/plans/ directory or any plan file, so for both, findPlanForPhase returns null, loadPhaseScopes sets phase-1 to null, and the line-483 guard skips phase-1 entirely - loadVisualApprovalLine, and therefore both tasks' new catch blocks, is never invoked by either fixture regardless of implementation correctness. res.stderr is the empty string in both runs, so Task 2's assert.match(res.stderr, /warning: could not read .*visual-approval\.jsonl/i, ...) (plan line 244) and Task 3's assert.match(res.stderr, /warning: could not parse .*visual-approval\.jsonl/i, ...) (plan line 293) both throw AssertionError unconditionally - an always-FAIL gate, the mirror image of the always-PASS defect this check normally guards against, and worse: it blocks even a correct implementation from ever landing. Consequence differs by task: Task 2's underlying fix is still validated correctly elsewhere - Level 3(b) fixture C (plan lines 363-366) does include the missing precondition (mkdirSync '.../PRPs/plans' + a plan file containing '| phase_scope | visual |') before layering the same directory-at-visual-approval.jsonl EISDIR scenario, and correctly asserts the could-not-read warning - so only Task 2's own per-task VALIDATE is broken, not plan-wide coverage of AC-A1/AC-A2 for that site. Task 3 has no such safety net: no command anywhere in the plan (not Task 3's own VALIDATE; not Level 1; not Level 2, whose existing figma-visual-first-track-phase7.test.mjs AC-A3 test explicitly declines to assert on stderr per its own comment at lines 507-513; not Level 3(a); not Level 3(b), whose 3 cases A/B/C cover only the absence path, Task 1's catch, and Task 2's catch) ever exercises the JSON.parse catch (source lines 239-243) with the phase_scope precondition met. AC-A1 and AC-A2 are therefore completely unvalidated for the JSON.parse catch site as this plan is currently written. Fix: add the same plan-file precondition Level 3(b) fixture C already uses (mkdirSync '.../PRPs/plans' recursive + writeFileSync a phase-1 plan with a phase_scope row) to both Task 2's and Task 3's VALIDATE fixtures before their spawnSync call, and give the JSON.parse catch at least one working validation somewhere in the plan (fixing Task 3's own fixture is sufficient; a 4th Level 3(b) case is a reasonable alternative).
